title: A Last Meal, Betrayal and Arrest
overview: In his final hours before his death, Jesus is anointed by a woman, shares a last Passover meal with his followers, prays in anguish, is betrayed and arrested, is condemned by the council, and is denied by his closest friend.

parts.label: A plot and a costly gift (vv. 1-11)
parts.note: The religious leaders want Jesus dead but fear a riot among the festival crowds, while a woman pours perfume worth about a year's wages over his head. When others call it waste, Jesus says she has prepared his body for burial ahead of time, and right after this Judas, one of his twelve closest followers, offers to hand him over for money.

parts.label: The Passover meal (vv. 12-21)
parts.note: Passover was the yearly meal remembering Israel's escape from slavery in Egypt, eaten with a sacrificed lamb and flat bread made without yeast. At the table Jesus says one of the twelve eating from the same bowl will betray him, and in that culture sharing a meal made such a betrayal especially deep.

parts.label: Bread and cup (vv. 22-26)
parts.note: Jesus links the bread to his body and the wine to his blood sealing a covenant, a binding agreement between God and people, echoing how Moses once sealed one with blood. Christians read this as the start of communion, the meal churches still share.

parts.label: Warning and prayer in Gethsemane (vv. 27-42)
parts.note: Jesus quotes the prophet Zechariah to say his friends will scatter, and Peter swears he never will. In a garden Jesus, overwhelmed with grief, asks God, whom he calls Abba, the Aramaic word for father, to take away the 'cup' of suffering ahead of him, yet he accepts God's will while his friends keep falling asleep.

parts.label: Arrested at night (vv. 43-52)
parts.note: Judas identifies Jesus with a kiss, a usual greeting for a teacher, and an armed crowd seizes him while one follower cuts off a servant's ear. Everyone runs, including a young man who escapes naked, and no one knows who he was, though some have guessed it was the writer of this book.

parts.label: Trial and Peter's denial (vv. 53-72)
parts.note: Before the Sanhedrin, the ruling Jewish council, the witnesses contradict each other until Jesus openly says he is the Messiah, using images from Daniel and the Psalms, and the high priest tears his robe to show he hears it as an insult to God. Meanwhile Peter, pressed by bystanders who say he must be one of them because he is from Galilee, denies knowing Jesus three times and breaks down weeping when the rooster crows.

disagreement: Christians differ on what Jesus meant by 'this is my body' and 'this is my blood': some believe he is truly present in the bread and wine, while others see the meal as a symbol and remembrance.
think: When have you promised more than you could actually carry through, and what happened afterward?
